nodes.label: Fixed horizontal louvers
nodes.description: Permanent horizontal fins above windows. Best for south facades. Sized for latitude 41°N to block summer sun above 60° altitude while admitting winter sun below 30°. Overhang depth = window height × tan(90° - 60° - lat).
nodes.performance_note: Reduces solar heat gain by 50–80% on south facades. Source: Szokolay 2004 §3.4.

nodes.label: External operable blinds or shutters
nodes.description: User-controlled external roller blinds or venetian shutters. More flexible than fixed louvers — can be opened in winter or for daylight. Best for E and W facades where sun angle varies.
nodes.performance_note: Can reduce solar gain by up to 90% when closed. Source: CIBSE Guide A 2015, Table 6.5.

nodes.label: Vegetated trellis / green facade
nodes.description: Climbing plants on a structural frame 200–400mm from facade surface. Provides shading AND evapotranspiration cooling effect. Deciduous species preferred.
nodes.performance_note: Reduces surface temperature by 5–15°C. Source: Pérez et al. 2011, Renewable and Sustainable Energy Reviews 15(1):576–583.

nodes.label: Roof overhangs / cantilevered balconies
nodes.description: Horizontal projection from the building facade. At lat 41°N, summer noon altitude ≈ 72°, so D ≈ H_window × 0.32 for full shading at summer solstice noon.

nodes.label: Through-building cross-ventilation
nodes.description: Open windows on windward and leeward facades simultaneously. Inlet on prevailing wind side (NE/N for Barcelona), outlet on opposite side. Inlet area should be 60–70% of outlet area. Source: CIBSE AM10:2005 §3.3.

nodes.label: Internal courtyard for ventilation
nodes.description: Central courtyard creates pressure differential driving cross-ventilation. Courtyard width : height ratio should be 1:1 to 2:1.

nodes.label: Wing walls to direct airflow
nodes.description: Vertical fins flanking windows on windward facade to capture oblique wind. Fin projection = 0.5–1.0 × window width.
nodes.suitable_for: facades where wind is oblique (>30° from normal)
nodes.performance_note: Increases inlet velocity by 30–50%. Source: Givoni 1994 Ch.4.

nodes.label: Exposed concrete or masonry internal surfaces
nodes.description: Leave internal face of concrete walls or floor slabs unfinished or with thin plaster. Insulation must be placed externally. Minimum 150mm concrete for effective thermal lag. Thermal admittance > 3 W/m²K required.
nodes.performance_note: Shifts peak indoor temperature by 4–6 hours. Source: Balaras 1996 §3.

nodes.label: Phase change material (PCM) panels
nodes.description: Microencapsulated PCM integrated into plasterboard or ceiling tiles. Melting point 23–26°C for Barcelona summer. Typical capacity: 14–30 MJ/m³.
nodes.performance_note: Reduces peak temperature by 2–4°C in lightweight buildings. Source: Cabeza et al. 2011, Energy and Buildings 43(6):1523–1533.

nodes.label: Trombe wall (thermal storage wall)
nodes.description: South-facing heavy masonry wall (300–400mm) with glazing 50–150mm in front. In Barcelona MUST be shaded in summer to prevent overheating.

nodes.label: Secure operable windows for night ventilation
nodes.description: Replace fixed glazing with tilt-and-turn or pivot windows. Install lockable ventilation position (10–15° opening) for security. Inlet near floor level, outlet near ceiling. Target: >5% of floor area operable.

nodes.label: Automated roof ventilators / clerestory openings
nodes.description: Motorised roof vents open automatically when outdoor temp drops below 22°C after sunset. Stack effect assists flow even in calm conditions.
nodes.performance_note: Stack ventilation adds 1–3 ACH at zero wind. Source: Santamouris 1996 §9.4.

nodes.label: Wind tower / cool tower
nodes.description: Vertical tower above roof captures wind and directs it downward. Effective in Barcelona's sea breeze regime when wind speed > 1.5 m/s.
nodes.performance_note: Passive — no energy consumption. Source: Givoni 1994 Ch.9.

nodes.label: Extensive sedum mat (50–100mm substrate)
nodes.description: Lightweight (60–120 kg/m²), low maintenance, drought-tolerant sedum. Minimum substrate depth 50mm. Irrigation not required after establishment.
nodes.performance_note: Reduces roof surface temperature by 20–30°C vs bare membrane. Source: Getter & Rowe 2006 §4.

nodes.label: Semi-intensive herbaceous green roof (150–250mm)
nodes.description: Medium substrate depth, wider plant palette. Better evapotranspiration than sedum. Requires occasional irrigation in Barcelona's dry summers. Load: 120–200 kg/m².

nodes.label: Green roof combined with photovoltaic panels
nodes.description: Bifacial PV panels elevated 300–500mm above green roof substrate. Green roof reduces ambient temperature (improves PV efficiency 3–5%). PV panels shade substrate (reduces irrigation need).

edges.note: Shading reduces solar gain, lowering indoor temp, increasing ventilation effectiveness. Source: Evola et al. 2017.
Compatible — shading reduces peak load that mass must handle.
Thermal mass absorbs daytime heat; night purge discharges it. Combined effect > sum of parts. Source: Balaras 1996 §4.
Compatible — heavy construction does not impede ventilation.
